entries.title: Inside the loop: Five AI attack frameworks that never ask permission
entries.description: Five agentic offensive frameworks act in bursts of two to 25 seconds, and none enforces authorization in code. What ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, Cairn, PentAGI, and HexStrike leave in your telemetry, and the ES|QL hunt that catches them.

entries.title: 56 AWS API calls in 141 milliseconds: Inside an AI-run intrusion
entries.description: A CyberStrikeAI server spent 16 days in four AWS accounts using eight identities, and the CloudTrail record shows why six detection rules each caught only part of it.

entries.title: Ransomware at the hypervisor layer: how attackers use ESXi and vCenter features for malicious purposes
entries.description: Kaspersky experts analyze a recent ransomware incident and discuss why the hypervisor layer remains difficult to monitor, what common access paths adversaries use to reach it, and how to protect your ESXi systems.

entries.title: LABScon26 Replay | Let’s Get Physical: Why Cybersecurity Needs Hardware-Based Security to Survive AI
entries.description: Adyen’s Dino Dai Zovi shows how hardware security proven in payments can contain AI-driven attacks, even when vulnerabilities cannot be patched.

entries.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation on Check Point Gateway
entries.description: We have now confirmed that, in late October 2026, approximately one week after a security fix became available, activity originating from 130.94.19[.]204 targeted Israeli organizations through vulnerable Mobile Access portals on Check Point Security Gateways. Evidence suggested some cases of a successful compromise, with exploitation activity consistent with PHP2Shell, associated with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.

entries.title: 0% GPU utilization: How SANSAR hides Linux cryptomining
entries.description: Elastic Security Labs analyzes SANSAR, a Linux cryptomining orchestrator that manages miners over Tor, alongside a kernel rootkit, GPU monitoring hooks and a backdoor that retrieves its C2 address from Ethereum.

entries.title: Transcending the trust boundaries: how a cloud pentest works
entries.description: This is the first article in a series on cloud penetration testing. We'll cover the three cloud layers (External, Overlay, and Underlay), common architectures (OpenStack and Kubernetes), typical attack chains, and real-world incidents.

entries.title: Citrus Ransomware: VLESS for traffic, Sn00py for encryption, and LLMs lending a hand
entries.description: We break down the Citrus Ransomware group's attacks: the attackers' TTPs and tooling, including VLESS traffic tunneling and LLM use, plus their links to Toy Ghouls.

entries.title: Not All That Glitters Is Gold: Tracking CopperDragon’s Sparrow Framework Around the Globe
entries.description: Over the past year, Check Point Research investigated a series of intrusion campaigns targeting several dozens of high-profile organizations across Latin America, Asia, and Europe. These campaigns initially appeared to be independent operations, each using different backdoors, post-exploitation tools and operational pace.

entries.title: IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Non-mobile statistics
entries.description: Key trends and statistics on malware targeting Windows and macOS computers and Internet of Things (IoT) devices in Q3 2026.

entries.title: IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Mobile statistics
entries.description: Q3 2026 mobile threat statistics for Android malware, adware, and unwanted software, plus the most notable malware found during the quarter.

entries.title: 9th November – Threat Intelligence Report
entries.description: For the latest discoveries in cyber research for the week of 9th November, please download our Threat Intelligence Bulletin.

entries.title: Virtualization security: attack layers and misconfiguration impact
entries.description: A detailed breakdown of misconfigurations in virtual environment cybersecurity as shown by examples of ransomware cases on ESXi and Proxmox environments.

entries.title: Hacking on Autopilot: Inside ARTEX Cybercrime Campaigns
entries.description: ARTEX is a Chinese open-source, AI-powered penetration testing platform designed to help security teams assess systems they own or are authorized to test. It uses large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multiple AI agents that plan tests, run security tools, and record evidence of potential vulnerabilities. Its web dashboard brings together assets, testing progress, captured traffic, and findings, allowing users to monitor activity and guide the agents. By linking each investigation to specif

entries.title: ChatGPT Lockdown Mode Bypass: Phishing, Malware Delivery, and Silent Data Exfiltration
entries.description: Earlier this year, Check Point Research disclosed a security flaw in ChatGPT’s code-execution runtime that allowed sensitive conversation data to be silently exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server through DNS tunneling, a hidden outbound channel that bypassed the runtime’s network isolation. A fix for this issue was promptly deployed.

entries.title: The SOC Files 5: Ghost in the pipeline, or a fileless SharePoint breach by Storm-2603
entries.description: Kaspersky researchers analyze a complex fileless cyberattack by Storm-2603 involving ToolShell exploitation and subsequent runtime subversion, and discuss how to detect such intrusions.

entries.title: VerifiedIDA | Making LLM-Driven Reverse Engineering Inspectable, Continuable and Reusable
entries.description: LLM reverse engineering scales only if analysis stays inspectable. A new standard and its open-source IDA Pro implementation tie annotations to evidence.

entries.title: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
entries.description: I tested vector search on 7,454 turns of my own agent sessions. One in seven sessions needed review, the agent’s reasoning carried more signal than the prompt, and the stored vectors answer questions nobody thought to ask at ingest.

entries.title: When trust becomes the payload: Inside the threats, etc quarterly report
entries.description: The newest threats, etc report details how adversaries are weaponizing trust across the entire enterprise stack, abusing everything from AI assistants and npm supply chains to identity flows and legitimate management tools.

entries.title: Defrost and Disrupt | An Assessment of Europe’s Refrigeration Attacks
entries.description: Store fridges and freezers warmed overnight in six countries on November 2-3. Russian-aligned groups are credible suspects, but attribution remains open.

entries.title: Free the Model, Sell the Gateway: Prompt Adware hidden in Jailbreak Bundles
entries.description: Check Point Research found a misconfigured webserver of a threat actor operating the Cobalt Strike framework. entries.title: MLEP in KICS for Networks 5.0: how machine learning helps track network behavior of OT devices
entries.description: We explain how Kaspersky Industrial CyberSecurity for Networks uses Machine Learning Event Processor (MLEP) technology to help take inventory of assets and detect anomalies in industrial networks.

entries.title: 2nd November – Threat Intelligence Report
entries.description: For the latest discoveries in cyber research for the week of 2nd November, please download our Threat Intelligence Bulletin.

entries.title: CyberStrikeAI in the wild: the use of AI in real-world attacks on organizations
entries.description: We analyze a series of attacks on educational institutions that were fully automated during the post-exploitation phase using the CyberStrikeAI penetration testing framework.
